title: Abhishuka (Pistachio)
body: In Ayurveda, Abhishuka is traditionally used to support physical stamina, nourish vital tissues, and calm dry Vata. Classical texts describe its seeds as having sweet and astringent tastes (Madhura and Kashaya Rasa), heavy and unctuous qualities (Guru and Snigdha Guna), heating energy (Ushna Virya), and a sweet post-digestive effect (Madhura Vipaka). Botanical name Pistacia vera. Rasa Madhura, Kashaya; guna Guru, Snigdha; virya Ushna; vipaka Madhura. Balances Vata; may increase Pitta, Kapha.

title: Muranji (Konkan Moringa)
body: In Ayurveda, Muranji is traditionally used to support deep channel clearing and melt dense internal accumulations. Classical texts describe its bark, roots, and seeds as having pungent and bitter tastes (Katu and Tikta Rasa), light, dry, and sharp qualities (Laghu, Ruksha, and Tikshna Guna), and heating energy (Ushna Virya), effectively pacifying Vata and Kapha. Botanical name Moringa concanensis. Rasa Katu, Tikta; guna Laghu, Ruksha, Tikshna; virya Ushna; vipaka Katu. Balances Vata, Kapha; may increase Pitta.

title: Mayaphala (Magic Nut / Oak Gall)
body: In Ayurveda, Mayaphala is traditionally used to support firm tissue tone, maintain fluid balance, and soothe mucous membranes. Classical texts describe the fruit gall as possessing a dominant astringent taste (Kashaya Rasa), light and dry qualities (Laghu and Ruksha Guna), and cooling potency (Sheeta Virya), which strongly balance Pitta and Kapha doshas. Botanical name Quercus infectoria. Rasa Kashaya; guna Laghu, Ruksha; virya Sheeta; vipaka Katu. Balances Pitta, Kapha; may increase Vata.

title: Kankra (Large-leafed Mangrove)
body: In Ayurveda, Kankra is traditionally used to support mucosal integrity and bind excessive fluids within internal pathways. Classical texts describe its bark as having astringent and bitter tastes (Kashaya and Tikta Rasa), light and dry qualities (Laghu and Ruksha Guna), and cooling energy (Sheeta Virya), serving to effectively pacify Pitta and Kapha. Botanical name Bruguiera gymnorhiza. Rasa Kashaya, Tikta; guna Laghu, Ruksha; virya Sheeta; vipaka Katu. Balances Pitta, Kapha; may increase Vata.

title: Sadapushpi (Madagascar Periwinkle)
body: In Ayurveda, Sadapushpi is traditionally used to balance internal metabolic heat and clear excess channel fluid. Classical texts describe its leaves and roots as possessing a bitter taste (Tikta Rasa), light and dry qualities (Laghu and Ruksha Guna), cooling potency (Sheeta Virya), and a pungent post-digestive effect (Katu Vipaka), which balance Pitta and Kapha. Botanical name Catharanthus roseus. Rasa Tikta; guna Laghu, Ruksha; virya Sheeta; vipaka Katu. Balances Pitta, Kapha; may increase Vata.

title: Sahachara (Porcupine Flower)
body: In Ayurveda, Sahachara is traditionally used to support lower body movement, joint flexibility, and neurological strength. Classical texts describe the whole plant and root as having bitter and sweet tastes (Tikta and Madhura Rasa), light and smooth qualities (Laghu and Snigdha Guna), and heating potency (Ushna Virya), making it ideal for balancing Vata and Kapha. Botanical name Barleria prionitis. Rasa Tikta, Madhura; guna Laghu, Snigdha; virya Ushna; vipaka Katu. Balances Vata, Kapha; may increase Pitta.
